chunks: My father (may Allah has mercy on him said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) wrote to some of his Shi'ites in Baghdad:
In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
May Allah guard us and you from the trial; if He does, then it is a great bounty. And if He does not, then it is a disaster.
We consider that argument regarding the Qur'an is an innovation in which both the questioner and the answerer share.
The questioner engages in what is not his due, and the answerer is constrained to answer what is not correct.
There is no creator except Allah, the Mighty and High. Anything other than Him is created.
The Qur'an is the Word of Allah. Do not make a name for it from your own self or you will be among the astray.
May Allah count us and you among those who fear their Lord in the unseen and are apprehensive of the Hour.
ai.seo_question: What is the status of the Qur'an according to Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) and why is argumentation about it considered an innovation?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) writes to his followers in Baghdad to clarify the ontological status of the Qur'an, warning against the innovation of treating it as a created entity or a separate name distinct from Allah's essence. He emphasizes that while Allah is the sole Creator, the Qur'an is His uncreated Speech, and excessive dialectical argumentation often leads both parties into theological error. This letter serves as a key text in the Shia tradition for understanding the balance between affirming the Qur'an as divine speech while avoiding the extremes of tashbih (anthropomorphism) and ta'til (denial).
